state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: To determine if the range changes when all values are changed by the same amount, remember that the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values. Think about how changing all the plant heights by the same amount would impact the highest and lowest values. Check your calculation with this in mind.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so if all the plants grow by 3 cm, then both the tallest and shortest would grow by 3 cm, so the difference between them would stay the same... but wait, does that mean Katie is right and Tom is wrong then? I'm confused because I thought cutting them in half would change the range, but now I'm not sure.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: To clarify, changing all values by the same amount affects both the highest and lowest values equally, keeping the difference between them the same. This means that both Tom and Katie are correct in this scenario. Remember, the range is determined by the difference between the highest and lowest values.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides mathematically incorrect information (claiming both Tom and Katie are correct when only Katie is right, since halving changes the range while adding a constant doesn't), fails to address the core misconception about proportional vs. additive changes, and the student ends confused rather than understanding the distinction.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides conceptual explanations about how range works rather than stating explicit procedures or showing worked steps with actual calculations, and does not directly correct the student's procedural error of miscalculating what happens when values are halved.
